fable.w: This section only amends existing provisions to add authorized appropriation amounts for fiscal years 1980 through 1982. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only amends appropriations provisions by adding dollar amounts for fiscal years 1980 through 1982. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory committee, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The underlying sections may involve outside entities elsewhere, but nothing in this text brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to appropriation levels for specific fiscal years. It does not mention any consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory bodies involving parties outside the federal government. It is purely a budgetary provision.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1516(d)(1) (as amended by section 106) is amended— (1) by striking out “and” after “1976,”, and (2) by inserting before the period the following: “, $150,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980, $165,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1981, and $185,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1982”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because these are appropriations for specific programs, they implicitly involve public participation through the programs themselves. However, the text itself only lists dollar amounts and fiscal years. It does not describe any process of consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties. The definition requires the section itself to involve participation, not just fund activities that might elsewhere involve it.
